title: Modi Inaugurates Bengaluru Metro Pink Line Stretch, Public Rides From November 14
excerpt: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar flagged off the 7.5-km Kalena Agrahara to S.G. Palya section, taking Bengaluru's metro network past 100 km.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday inaugurated the 7.5-km elevated stretch of Bengaluru's Namma Metro Pink Line from Kalena Agrahara to S.G. Palya.
  • The stretch cost about Rs 3,470 crore, has six stations, and opens to the public from 6 am on Saturday, November 14.
  • The opening pushes Bengaluru's operational metro network past 100 km; the full Pink Line will be 21.25 km with 18 stations.
  • The Jayadeva Hospital station will provide an interchange with the Yellow Line.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday inaugurated the elevated stretch of Bengaluru's Namma Metro Pink Line from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere, built at a cost of around Rs 3,470 crore, and travelled on the new service with Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar.

Modi and Shivakumar together flagged off the services, bought separate tickets from the counter, and rode the train, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. Governor Sudha Yadav, Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya and Minister Krishna Byre Gowda also travelled on the train.

Six stations on Bannerghatta Road

The 7.5-km elevated section runs from Kalena Agrahara to S.G. Palya, formerly Tavarekere, along Bannerghatta Road. Its six stations are Kalena Agrahara, Hulimavu, Bilekahalli-IIMB, N.S. Palya-J.P. Nagar 4th Phase, Jayadeva Hospital and S.G. Palya, according to an IANS report carried by hi INDiA.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DfrgO9qE3S7/

At the flag-off at S.G. Palya station, Modi asked Shivakumar, who was standing at a distance, to join him, held his hand and invited him to stand alongside before both waved the green flag, the IANS report said. Modi later handed the flag to Governor Yadav.

Officials of the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited briefed the prime minister on the project. Shivakumar explained the advantage of a double-decker elevated corridor carrying both a metro line and a flyover to ease traffic congestion, BusinessLine reported.

"The inauguration of the 7.5-km elevated stretch of Namma Metro's Pink Line, connecting Kalena Agrahara to S.G. Palya through six stations, will make daily travel easier for people."

— D.K. Shivakumar, Karnataka Chief Minister

Network past 100 km, full line still to come

The inauguration pushed Bengaluru's operational metro network past the 100-kilometre milestone. Metro services on the new stretch will open to the public from Saturday, November 14, with services from 6 am, officials said.

The full Pink Line will span 21.25 km with 18 stations, connecting Kalena Agrahara in south Bengaluru to Nagawara in the north. The elevated corridor inaugurated on Friday has six stations, while the underground section, with 12 stations, is still under construction, BusinessLine reported.

The Jayadeva Hospital station will provide an interchange with the Yellow Line, and officials said the elevated section is expected to connect with the Electronic City line at Jayadeva station. The new stretch is expected to enhance urban connectivity, ease daily commuting, reduce travel time and strengthen public transport in Bengaluru, according to an official statement cited by BusinessLine.

Krishna Byre Gowda said a city that powers the nation must have infrastructure to match its ambitions, and that meeting Bengaluru's mobility needs requires a shared commitment from both the state and the Centre, according to the IANS report.
